question: What is the primary goal of health education?

options.A: Empowering people to improve their health

explanation: Health education focuses on giving individuals and communities the knowledge and tools they need to improve their own health outcomes. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h1)

question: Why is it so helpful for a nurse to explain health concepts in local languages?

options.A: It replaces the need for clinical diagnosis
options.B: It reduces the cost of importing medical textbooks
options.C: It speeds up the process of writing patient case notes
options.D: It helps patients understand and apply health practices

explanation: When you speak in familiar terms, patients truly grasp the message and can easily act on it. Communication is key to great nursing! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h1)

question: Which objective of health education deals with building practical self-care skills like handwashing?
explanation: The psychodynamic (or behavioral) objective focuses on the physical execution of practical skills—getting hands-on with procedures like wound care. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h2)

question: A nurse teaches mothers why immunization prevents killer childhood diseases. Which learning domain is this mainly addressing?
explanation: Teaching the reasons behind disease prevention and building mental understanding targets the cognitive domain of knowledge. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h2)

question: What does 'active participation' mean when conducting a community health session?

options.A: Only community leaders are allowed to ask questions
options.B: The community is involved rather than just listening passively
options.C: Nurses must do all the talking during every session
options.D: Patients are required to pay a fee before learning

explanation: Active participation means learners engage directly with the material through questions and actions, which helps them remember and change behaviors better. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h3)

question: Why should nurses always focus on 'felt needs' (real problems the community faces daily) when planning education?

options.A: It guarantees immediate financial funding from donors
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to prepare visual aids
options.C: Learners pay closer attention to problems they actually experience
options.D: Government policy requires ignoring community complaints

explanation: People naturally care more about health issues affecting their everyday lives than abstract or distant theories. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h3)

question: Which area of health education focuses on workplace safety and protective gear for workers?
explanation: Occupational health targets workers in factories, offices, or farms to prevent job-related injuries and illnesses. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h4)

question: A student nurse organizes a session on safe waste disposal and clean water sources for a rural village. Which scope of health education does this fall under?
explanation: Waste disposal, sanitation, and clean water are core components of environmental health education. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h4)

question: In the Health Belief Model, what do we mean by 'perceived susceptibility'?

options.A: A reminder from a family member to visit the clinic
options.B: Believing one is at risk for a health problem
options.C: The financial cost of buying hospital drugs
options.D: Thinking a disease has no cure at all

explanation: Perceived susceptibility is simply a person's mindset of 'Could this sickness happen to me?' It's about personal vulnerability. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h5)

question: A patient refuses malaria treatment because they feel the drugs are too expensive and far away. In the Health Belief Model, what is this called?
explanation: Perceived barriers are the hurdles, costs, or inconveniences that make someone hesitant to take healthy actions. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h5)

question: Which health education approach uses face-to-face counseling and home visits?
explanation: The individual approach gives personalized education through direct one-on-one time, like patient counseling or home visits. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h6)

question: What is a major limitation of using radio broadcasts for community health education?

options.A: It can only be used inside hospital wards
options.B: It completely replaces the need for clinical nurses
options.C: It is impossible for illiterate people to ever hear a radio
options.D: It lacks two-way interaction and personalized feedback

explanation: While radio reaches many people, listeners can't ask questions right away or get personalized answers the way they can with a nurse present. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h6)

question: What is the very first step a nurse must take when planning a community health program?
explanation: Always assess first! You need to know what problems actually exist in the community before you can plan how to help. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h7)

question: Why is it so important to involve community members during the planning stage of a health program?

options.A: It ensures the program respects local culture and actual needs
options.B: It guarantees that funding will come from international donors
options.C: It removes the need for any evaluation at the end
options.D: It allows the nurse to avoid attending community meetings

explanation: When people help plan their own health programs, they take ownership and the project is much more likely to succeed. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge to health education in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of advanced medical equipment in every village
options.C: Cultural and traditional beliefs regarding illness
options.D: Language barriers and low literacy rates

explanation: Advanced equipment is definitely not overflowing in rural clinics! Resource shortages are the real hurdle, making this option false. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h8)

question: How can poverty make health education harder to put into practice?

options.A: It automatically cures all infectious diseases
options.B: Patients may struggle to afford recommended foods or medications
options.C: It prevents community members from gathering together
options.D: It stops nurses from speaking local languages

explanation: Financial hardship makes it tough for patients to follow health advice that requires buying prescribed drugs or specific nutritious foods. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h8)

question: When is a formative evaluation carried out during a health education program?

options.A: Only when funding is being audited
options.B: During the program for ongoing feedback
options.C: Years after the program has ended completely
options.D: Before any planning or assessment begins

explanation: Formative evaluation happens while the program is running so you can spot issues and fix them on the fly! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h9)

question: A nurse checks if a school handwashing campaign successfully reduced diarrhea cases over the term. What kind of evaluation is this?
explanation: Summative evaluation looks at the final results and overall impact after the whole educational program has wrapped up. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h9)
